name: f1-core-v1
target_failure: Weaker readers executing contradictory or unused text: F1's late-run caution overrides its own Lay-low guard, and most of its labels are never used.
hypothesis: F1's lead on Haiku comes from a small core that the actor actually executes: the Act test, repair the weakest, the story filter, Act-first Energy and a main action aimed at the weakest gap. The rest is either unused or works against that core. In 809 decisions of the 4 F1 digests, notes use the Watch and Fine labels 1% and 0% of the time, cite the Output-after-a-C-or-D rule 1% and 'spread' 0%, and Skill learning or High-intensity work appears in 0 of 64 Energy phases. The late-run caution is cited in 11% of notes from mid-run on and produced all 5 of F1's Lay-low main actions, every one at full Health, against F1's own rule 'Lay low only when Health is Act'; the weakest F1 game (Q 57.1, four Cs) took 4 of them. Keeping only the executed core (486 to 284 words) keeps F1's completion and score on Haiku, removes the contradiction a weaker reader resolves towards caution, and costs fewer tokens on every turn.
change: Kept, compressed: the turn loop; the Act definition without 'Output after a C or D review'; F1's Watch band renamed Weakest with the same definition (a falling statistic, else the lowest of Skill, Network and Output); the three story rules; the Energy order (Act first, then lift the weakest with the Health guard on Skill learning and High-intensity work, Defuse legacy risk after an accumulated or legacy risk warning, spend all Energy); the main-action rule with its Lay-low guard. Removed: the ending-rationale paragraph; the Fine band; the pointer to energy_cost, status_updates and remaining_energy; 'spread points'; 'repeat a main action only while the same gap persists'; the whole 'Across the run' section (same discipline, promotion rationale, Output after a C or D, late-run caution; the last is also wording new Skills may not use). Skill name unchanged. 284 words against 486.
predicted_behaviour: Against F1 in the same 4-run Haiku screen: no Lay low and reduce risk main action while Health is not Act (parent 5 of 5 at full Health) and no late-run or final-months caution in notes (parent 11% of notes); Apply for a key project in at least the parent's share of main actions (75%) and the same Energy mix otherwise (Defuse legacy risk about 40% of phases, Prepare report materials about 70%, Health recovery about 40%); promotion at review 1 in at least 3 of 4 runs (parent 4 of 4 digests); completed runs reach the parent's top Level at least as often; notes no longer than the parent's (mean about 124 characters) and fewer input tokens per decision; at least 3 of 4 runs complete (parent 7 of 8).
refutation: Refuted if 2 or more of the 4 runs exit early, or the 4-run mean quantitative_score is more than 8 points below the parent's 8-run mean (58.9), or the block decision places it below the parent under the dormant rule. Manipulation fails if Lay low at full Health or late-run caution still appears in most runs (the actor brings the caution itself), or if the key-project share falls below the parent's (the removed text was steering the main action). If the score falls while behaviour matches the parent, a removed rule mattered: restore the 'Across the run' section first, without its late-run line (P20 decision rule).
notes: Block 5 (decision #142), F1 child 1 of 2. Base of a nested ladder: f1-core-v1 (subtraction) and f1-risk-signal-v1 (this text plus one risk rule), with the stall slot f1-status-line-v1 (the same rules as f1-risk-signal-v1 as a status line). f1-core-v1 against F1 isolates the subtraction; the next rung isolates the risk trigger. The 'late in the run' line had to go in every child (wording rule for new Skills); here it is part of the hypothesis. No numbers, months or calendar triggers; grades and the 0–10 range are published. Evidence and counts in lab/reports/cloud-run-diagnostics/block5-generation.md.
